title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Grothendieck fixes S, a smooth curve X/S (relative curve f: X -> S) and a section t. Write X* for the complement of t. He compares two categories.

- First category: triples (X', t', G). Here X' -> X is a tame G-cover, étale over X*, with a marked section t' over t where it is ramified.
- Second category: systems (G, n, xi, i, T, k). Here G is a (commutative) finite flat group scheme on S. The class xi lies in H^0(S, R^1 f_*(G on X*)) and has local monodromy at t that is tamely ramified of order n. The map i: mu_{n,S} -> G is a monomorphism (the inertia at t). T is an invertible O_S-module, and k: T^{otimes n} ≅ T_{X/S,t} is an isomorphism with the tangent (normal) line of the section t.

This page opens by asserting that the canonical functor from the first category to the second is an equivalence of categories.

The mechanism, in modern terms. If X' -> X is totally ramified of index n along t' over t, the n-th power map on conormal lines gives a canonical isomorphism T_{X',t'}^{otimes n} ≅ T_{X,t}. So the cover produces an n-th root of the tangent line of t.

Conversely, fix the global section xi of R^1 f_*. Locally on S it lifts to a torsor over X*. The lifts form a gerbe banded by G (f_* G = G, since the fibres of X* are connected). The claim is that, once the inertia is fixed, this gerbe is identified with the gerbe of n-th roots of T_{X,t}.

Special case mu_2, n = 2, residue characteristics not 2. Here the objects are quadratic Kummer covers X' of X, étale over X*, totally ramified along t. For fixed xi in H^0(S, R^1 f_* mu_2) satisfying the total-ramification condition, the groupoid of such covers is equivalent to the groupoid of pairs (T, k) with T^{otimes 2} ≅ T_{X,t}. This is a mu_2-gerbe of square roots. As a corollary, the Leray obstruction d_2(xi) in H^2(S, mu_2) equals the Kummer class of the line bundle T_{X,t}.

Application to elliptic curves. Take X = Sigma_J^*, where:
- J is the finite étale cubic S-scheme of nonzero 2-torsion points;
- Sigma_J is the J-marked projective line E/{±1};
- Sigma_J^* is Sigma_J minus the degree-3 divisor D_J.
Then X' is E minus its nonzero 2-torsion, and t is the image of the zero section.

The next page states the consequence: an elliptic curve over S (2 invertible) is equivalent to the data (J, a point t in Sigma_J^*, a line T, an iso T^{otimes 2} ≅ T_{Sigma,t}). The automorphism -1 of E corresponds to -1 on T. This is a description of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a mu_2-gerbe of square roots of the tangent line, over the stack of P^1's with a marked étale cubic divisor and an extra point. It is a stacky Legendre/Weierstrass description.
errors: The equivalence implicitly needs G commutative (or a non-abelian H^1 formalism), fibres of X* connected, and tameness; these are not all stated explicitly.
'étales au dessus de X' should read 'étale above X*' (the complement of t); as written it contradicts total ramification along t.
Morphisms when n changes (mu_n -> mu_{n1}, lambda -> lambda^{n/n1}) are only sketched on the previous page; the definition of morphisms in the second category is left ad hoc.

ideas.what: Tame G-covers of a curve with a section, totally ramified along it, correspond to (class in R^1 f_*, inertia mu_n -> G, n-th root of the tangent line of the section)
ideas.modern_name: Root stacks / twisted curves; gerbe of liftings of a section of R^1 f_*; tangential data at a branch point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group, 1971); Abramovich–Vistoli, Cadman, Olsson (root stacks and twisted curves, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Tame ramification in SGA1/Grothendieck–Murre, but not this gerbe formulation

ideas.what: Double covers with fixed Kummer class form a mu_2-gerbe equal to the gerbe of square roots of T_{X,t}; hence d_2(xi) equals the Kummer class of T_{X,t}
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe of square roots; Kummer obstruction in the Leray spectral sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Arsie–Vistoli, stacks of cyclic covers (2004)

ideas.what: M_{1,1}[1/2] described as a mu_2-gerbe of square roots of the tangent line at t over (J-marked P^1, point t off D_J)
ideas.modern_name: Stacky Weierstrass/Legendre description of M_{1,1}; M_{1,1} as a mu_2-gerbe over a quotient of M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; hyperelliptic stacks as gerbes (Arsie–Vistoli; Bertin, Beauville, et al.)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and M_{0,4} but not this construction explicitly

missed.claim: Grothendieck pins down the mu_2-gerbe M_{1,1} -> (P^1 with 3+1 points) concretely as square roots of the tangent line at the image of 0_E. This prefigures the use of tangential data at a marked point and the M_{1,1}/M_{0,4} comparison central to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory (Deligne's tangential base points, 1989). Here it appears in a moduli-stack form rather than a fundamental-group form.
missed.quote: la catégorie des revêtements correspondants ... est équivalente à celle des couples (J, k) d'un Module inversible J sur S, et d'un iso J^{⊗2} ≃ T_{X,t}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, explicit gerbe-theoretic description of M_{1,1}[1/2] relative to M_{0,4}-type stacks. It is of historical interest for the Esquisse/Teichmüller tower programme, though the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The result is correct and elegant but standard by modern root-stack and cyclic-cover technology. Its interest is mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck around 1980–82 working with gerbes of tangent roots to describe M_{1,1}.
transcription_corrections: 'R^1 f_*(\mu_2 X^*)' should be R^1 f_*(\mu_{2,X^*}), i.e. mu_2 on the complement X* of t.
In '(J,k)' and 'J^{⊗2} ≃ J_{X,t}' the target is the tangent line T_{X,t}; the root module is written J/T in the manuscript, and the next page calls it T.

'(fibré en droites projectives associé au Module inversible J sur S)' is likely a misreading. J in Sigma_J is the étale cubic S-scheme of nonzero 2-torsion points, not an invertible module; the manuscript reads roughly '(J-marked projective line bundle ... tordue by J on S)'.
The line 'associé à un rev. elliptique X' comme X'/{±1}' is a struck first attempt, replaced by 'déduit d'une courbe elliptique X' comme X'/{±1}'.
